metaDescription: Dachshund vaccine schedule with core ages in weeks. Set reminders so Dachshund boosters are not missed.

bodySections.heading: Why timing matters for this schedule
paragraphs: Dachshund owners tracking 12-16 years lifespans still lose the mid-series booster more often than the first shot, and the unprotected gap after week 8 is where parvovirus risk concentrates for this puppy.
Use the 4-row Dachshund schedule as your only planning spine: 8 weeks (DA2PP / DHPP); 12 weeks (DA2PP / DHPP booster); 16 weeks (DA2PP / DHPP booster); 16 weeks (Rabies).

Temperament note for Dachshund handling: Curious hound; stairs and jumping are spinal risk management issues.. Schedule quieter appointment slots if that profile makes clinic visits harder, but do not skip the Dachshund dose.
Lifestyle add-ons stay off this Dachshund core list until your veterinarian maps exposure, so keep core dates sacred either way.

bodySections.heading: If a dose is missed or delayed
paragraphs: If your Dachshund misses the dose scheduled near week 12, call the clinic the same day with product names — do not restart the Dachshund series from memory.
The danger for a delayed Dachshund is the gap, not the embarrassment, because parvovirus pressure stays real for an under-vaccinated puppy even in clean-looking neighborhoods.
While waiting for the make-up DA2PP / DHPP visit, skip high-traffic dog parks / unknown-cat intros and keep the Dachshund away from unvaccinated animals.
After catch-up, rewrite reminders for the next Dachshund due date (7, 3, and 1 day prior) so the same miss does not recur.

faqs.question: When does the Dachshund core vaccine series usually finish?
faqs.answer: This breed record completes core vaccines around 16 weeks of age, with rabies timed per local law. Your clinic may adjust intervals for the individual puppy.

faqs.question: What should I do if my Dachshund misses a booster?
faqs.answer: Contact your veterinarian for a catch-up plan instead of restarting or skipping ahead. Keep prior dates handy and limit high-risk exposure until the series is current again.

faqs.question: Where can I read Dachshund health context beyond vaccines?
faqs.answer: See the Dachshund adult health guide for breed predispositions such as intervertebral disc disease (ivdd), then bring those notes to wellness and vaccine visits.
